title: Eco-Sensitive Zones: Rules, Disputes and Cases

cards.b:
Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs) are around protected areas and are a frequent Prelims and Mains theme because they touch courts, farmers and development. The 2022 Supreme Court order on a one-kilometre buffer made them a news topic again.

Know what an ESZ is, who notifies it and what is allowed.

An Eco-Sensitive Zone (also called Ecologically Fragile Area) is an area around a national park or wildlife sanctuary that works as a shock absorber. It eases the shift from a strictly protected core to areas of heavier use. It is not a legal term in the Wildlife (Protection) Act. The Centre notifies ESZs under Section 3(2)(v) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and Rule 5(1) of the 1986 Rules.

The National Wildlife Action Plan 2002-2016 asked for land around PAs to be notified as ESZ.

In 2002 the Wildlife Conservation Strategy said ESZs should reach up to 10 km around PAs. The MoEFCC guidelines (2011) say the width can vary from site to site, and where sensitive corridors or areas lie beyond 10 km, the ESZ may extend further. A Monitoring Committee and a Zonal Master Plan, prepared by the state, guide land use.

Activities are sorted into three groups:

  • Prohibited: commercial mining, sawmills, polluting industries, major hydroelectric projects, use of firewood commercially.
  • Regulated: tree felling, hotels and resorts, new roads, drawing of groundwater.
  • Promoted: rainwater harvesting, organic farming, renewable energy, eco-tourism.

cards.h: Supreme Court and the 1 km rule
cards.b:
In Goa Foundation v Union of India (2006) the Court directed that ESZ be notified around PAs. On 3 June 2022, in the T.N. Godavarman case, the Supreme Court ruled that every protected area must have a mandatory ESZ of at least 1 km from its boundary, and that mining is not allowed within the PA. Several states objected that villages and farms would be hit.

In April 2023 the Court modified its order: the 1 km rule would not apply where an ESZ was already notified or proposed under earlier guidelines, and the bar on mining within the PA stayed. The Court also gave relief for areas with existing homes and public use.

The EPA 1986 has also been used for named regions:

  • Doon Valley (1989).
  • Dahanu taluka, Maharashtra (1991), where an authority (the Dahanu Taluka Environment Protection Authority, 1996) checks projects.
  • Mahabaleshwar-Panchgani (2001) and Matheran (2003).
  • Bhagirathi Eco-Sensitive Zone, Uttarakhand, notified in 2012, covering about 100 km from Gaumukh to Uttarkashi. It affected small hydropower projects.

The Western Ghats ESA proposals (Gadgil 2011 and Kasturirangan 2013) are the largest of such attempts.

Think of the zones as rings. The core of a national park has no human use. The sanctuary allows limited activity. The ESZ regulates activity. Beyond lies general land use. ESZs also keep animals from straying into fields by managing land use at the edge, and they reduce noise, dust and light pollution close to the core.

Villagers fear bans on building, farming and wells and say they were not consulted. Developers and states say a blanket 1 km is rigid in dense places like Kerala, where thousands of homes lie within 1 km of PAs. Conservation groups say a thin buffer cannot stop encroachment, mining and roads.

The ESZ also lacks direct statutory backing in the WPA, so some experts want it added.

Kerala sought relief after the 2022 order as the 1 km rule would touch homes around many sanctuaries, including Wayanad. Goa and Karnataka have long-pending ESZ proposals around PAs. The Rajaji ESZ and the Corbett ESZ affect tourism. The notification process asks for a draft with a 60-day public comment and then final notification. About 2,000 or so ESZs are notified or proposed across India (a figure that changes).

• ESZ: notified under EPA 1986, not WPA.
  • 2011 MoEFCC guidelines: up to 10 km, flexible.
  • 3 June 2022: SC ordered 1 km minimum; April 2023: modified.
  • Bhagirathi ESZ: 2012.
  • Three lists: prohibited, regulated, promoted.

Prelims-style: "Eco-Sensitive Zones are notified under which Act?" (EPA 1986). "Which area is a Western Ghats-linked ecologically fragile area?"

Mains-style: "Eco-sensitive zones are essential yet controversial. Discuss." Structure: purpose; legal base; court orders; livelihood and development conflict; reform (participatory master plans, flexible width, statutory backing).
